test_title: PYST 04: RRB Group D Official Paper GS - (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is NOT true regarding the image formed by a concave lens?

(i) The image formed by a concave lens cannot be obtained on a screen.

(ii) The image formed by a concave lens can be obtained on a screen.

(iii) The image formed is always smaller in size in comparison to the size of the object.

(iv) The image formed is always bigger in size in comparison to the size of the object.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (i):** The image formed by a concave lens cannot be obtained on a screen. *This statement is correct.*

 
 
• The concave lens always forms a **virtual image**, which cannot be projected on a screen.
 
• The virtual image is formed on the same side as the object, and it appears to be upright.
 
 
 
• **Statement (ii):** The image formed by a concave lens can be obtained on a screen. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
 
• Since concave lenses form only virtual images, they cannot be captured on a screen.
 
• Images that can be obtained on a screen must be real, which is not possible with concave lenses.
 
 
 
• **Statement (iii):** The image formed is always smaller in size in comparison to the size of the object. *This statement is correct.*
 
 
• The concave lens produces a diminished (smaller) image, irrespective of the distance of the object from the lens.
 
• This property makes concave lenses useful in applications like peepholes in doors.
 
 
 
• **Statement (iv):** The image formed is always bigger in size in comparison to the size of the object. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
 
• The concave lens cannot form a magnified image. It always forms a reduced (smaller) image.
 
• Magnification greater than 1 is typically associated with convex lenses, not concave lenses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of a Concave Lens:**

 
 
• A concave lens is also known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges light rays that pass through it.
 
• The lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.
 
• It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**, regardless of the object's position.
 
• The focal length of a concave lens is considered negative because it is measured from the lens to the virtual focal point.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Lenses:**
 
 
• Used in **spectacles** for correcting nearsightedness (myopia).
 
• Used in **optical instruments** like telescopes and cameras as auxiliary lenses to manipulate image properties.
 
• Commonly used in **peepholes** in doors to provide a wide field of view.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Real and Virtual Images:**
 
 
• **Real Image:** Formed by actual convergence of light rays; can be obtained on a screen; inverted in nature.
 
• **Virtual Image:** Formed by the apparent divergence of light rays; cannot be obtained on a screen; upright in nature.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens vs. Convex Lens:**
 
 
• **Concave Lens:** Diverges light rays, forms virtual and diminished images.
 
• **Convex Lens:** Converges light rays, forms real and magnified images (depending on object position).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The lens formula is given by 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• **Magnification:** The magnification (M) of a lens is defined as M = v/u, and for concave lenses, it is always less than 1 (indicating a diminished image).
 
• **Sign Convention:** In lens calculations, distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, while those measured against it are negative.
